title: The Sky Still Runs the House
working_title: The Sky Still Runs the House
subtitle: Ancient astrology and the structures we still live in
based_on: the documented history of astral omen-reading, horoscopy, calendrics, mathematical astronomy, medicine, statecraft, print culture, and modern empirical testing across Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Hellenistic Mediterranean, India, China, the Islamic world, Europe, and Mesoamerica — an original narrative synthesis in the author's own words
author: Andries J. Greyling
protagonist: a sequence of watchers, scribes, calendar keepers, physicians, translators, printers, astronomers, clients, and sceptics who kept turning the sky into a human-readable structure
setting: Nineveh, Babylon, Alexandria, Ujjain, imperial China, Maya cities, Baghdad, European courts and print shops, and a twentieth-century psychology classroom, c. 1700 BCE-present
logline: Ancient astrology did not need to predict a modern personality correctly to change the modern world: it helped build durable ways of dividing time, mapping the sky, funding observation, running courts, recording cases, printing forecasts, and turning uncertainty into an interface — a history of what survived after the fate fell out.
genre: history of ideas / history of science / narrative nonfiction
blueprint: five parts and twenty-two short chapters: (I) Mesopotamian celestial omens become a data practice, a twelve-sign coordinate strip, and finally a private birth chart; (II) the system crosses borders and is remade in Hellenistic Egypt and India, while Chinese astral statecraft and Maya calendrical divination are treated as distinct systems rather than Western astrology in costume; (III) astral practice enters the week, medicine, courts, Islamic translation and observatory culture, and print; (IV) astronomy and astrology separate gradually, and predictive claims meet controlled testing and psychology; (V) a claim-by-claim audit separates direct inheritance, historical dependency, living tradition, and structural analogy.
market: readers of Bill Bryson, Sapiens, The Dawn of Everything, histories of science, cultural astronomy, and curious readers who want something more honest than either horoscope advocacy or a two-page debunking
status: DRAFT COMPLETE (22 chapters across 5 parts plus front/backmatter; ~18.5k single-shot manuscript, 2026-08-30)
tone: warm, plain-spoken, curious, and exact; respectful toward living traditions and historical actors without granting unsupported predictive claims; wonder first, jokes earned, causal claims labelled
dedication: For everyone who has ever looked up because the ground would not answer. And for the people who kept the count.
clearances: Historical figures are discussed through the public scholarly record. Living cultural practitioners appear only at the level of documented public traditions, not fictionalized scenes. No source prose is copied. The book distinguishes ancient systems that are historically connected from those that arose independently, and does not collapse living Maya, Indian, or Chinese practices into modern Western sun-sign astrology.
sensitivity_read: recommended before publication for the India, China, and living Maya chapters; the draft deliberately avoids declaring living traditions to be fossils or treating all astral practice as a single diffusion chain
